title: Test headless Codex single-Action run, OpenCode on failure (experiment fixture)
problem: Agents cannot run the Codex or OpenCode CLIs: they fail inside the agent sandbox and launching unsandboxed agents is refused. So nobody knows whether a headless provider session, started with the unattended command line Arcadia's launcher builds for a standing-policy launch, can finish one trivial governed Action with no human input. A fingerprint launch today runs the interactive TUI, which never exits, so this has to be proved by running the provider for real, on a disposable fixture, as the operator.
desired_effect: In a fresh Decision 0082 experiment workspace and a one-Action fixture repository (no remote) under a temporary directory, Arcadia prepares the Action (go --apply --agent codex with a seeded immutable build packet and a fresh experiment-only heartbeat), then the script runs Codex headless with the exact unattended argv Arcadia's shipped launch builder produces (codex exec --model ... --config model_reasoning_effort=... --sandbox workspace-write --cd <worktree> <brief>) for at most 15 minutes, teeing its output to a log. It then prints and records a PASS/FAIL table: the provider exited 0 within the cap, MARKER.md has the exact expected line, node scripts/check-fixture.mjs passes, a commit with the file exists on the candidate branch, and a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask was drafted that agent-ask preview accepts. It also reports whether the worktree's gitdir lies inside Codex's sandbox-writable roots and, as information only, what session reconcile makes of the finished Session (accepted_completion is unreachable in an experiment workspace because no worker exists). Only if Codex fails does it repeat the whole test on a fresh fixture with OpenCode (opencode run --model ...). Run it from /runs, or from a terminal: /Users/pmark/Dev/MR/Arcadia/arcadia/artifacts/generated/operator-scripts/test-headless-provider-single-action.sh run Expected duration: typically 2 to 10 minutes, at most about 35. Cost: uses your existing Codex (and only if Codex fails, OpenCode) plan; no separate spend.
preconditions: Run on the operator's own Mac, signed in: codex on PATH and codex login status succeeds (OpenCode: opencode on PATH and opencode auth list shows a credential, checked only if Codex fails)
Today is within Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18)
The Arcadia checkout this library belongs to has its dependencies installed (the test runs its CLI)
No other input is needed; nothing is read from or written to the live workspace except a read-only leak-check snapshot

parameters.--keep: Optional argument (terminal only; /runs passes none), or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1: keep the temporary experiment workspace, fixture and candidate worktree for inspection. The run logs and receipt are always kept.
parameters.ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: Optional environment variable: the per-provider cap in milliseconds (default 900000, fifteen minutes).

expected_duration: Typically 2 to 10 minutes. At most about 35 minutes: one 15-minute provider cap for Codex, one for OpenCode when Codex fails, plus about a minute of setup per provider.
cost_note: Uses the operator's existing Codex (and, only if Codex fails, OpenCode) plan: one short headless session each on a one-line task. No API key is read or entered and no separate spend is authorized or incurred.

does: Refuses before creating anything unless today is within Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18), the codex binary is on PATH and codex login status succeeds (OpenCode is checked with opencode auth list only if it is reached)

Creates a temporary directory, a fresh experiment workspace in it with arcadia init --profile experiment, and a one-Action fixture repository with no remote under that workspace's projects directory; every Arcadia command names that workspace explicitly and the live workspace is never addressed

Writes a freshly timestamped worker heartbeat file inside the experiment workspace only (the experiment guard forbids starting a worker), seeds one immutable build packet there, and prepares the candidate worktree with go --apply through a recording process boundary that starts nothing

Runs the provider CLI headless with the unattended argv built by the shipped launch builder, in the candidate worktree, with ARCADIA_WORKSPACE set in the provider's own environment to the experiment workspace (never exported in any shell) and the operator-script markers removed, for at most 15 minutes, killing its whole process group on timeout
Lets go --launch's ordinary read-only provider capacity query run (for Codex, codex app-server account/rateLimits/read), exactly as a real launch would
Takes a read-only live-workspace leak-check snapshot before and after, reported as information because other sessions legitimately write the live workspace

Writes run.log, one log per provider, a receipt.json (arcadia-operator-run-receipt-v1 with per-provider results and log paths) and, on failure, a failure-handoff.md under runs/<timestamp-pid>/, which are always kept
Removes the temporary directory at the end unless --keep or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1 is given
never_does: Never addresses, reads for any purpose but the leak-check snapshot, or writes the live martianrover workspace, and never exports ARCADIA_WORKSPACE
Never activates production, starts, stops or restarts a service or worker, installs the go-broker, or settles, merges, pushes or opens anything on GitHub

Never reads, writes or repairs provider global configuration or authentication (codex login, opencode auth login and their config files stay the operator's), and never installs software or enters a credential
Never registers a repository with a remote, and never touches the primary Arcadia checkout, other worktrees or any path outside its temporary directory and runs/<timestamp-pid>/
Never reports accepted_completion: with no worker in an experiment workspace it cannot be reached, so session reconcile output is information only

success.effect: At least one provider (Codex first) exited 0 within the cap, wrote and committed the expected MARKER.md, passed the fixture check and drafted a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask that preview accepts. The receipt records the table, the model, the exact command, the log paths and the gitdir finding.
success.next: Read receipt.json under runs/<timestamp-pid>/ in the operator-scripts directory. If Codex passed, headless Codex is viable for a standing-policy launch on this host; give the receipt (especially the gitdir finding) to Arcadia to decide the next Action. If only OpenCode passed, say so in the same handoff.

failure.effect: No provider passed every criterion, or a precondition refused. The script exits non-zero and writes receipt.json and failure-handoff.md with the table and the failing criterion for each provider, plus every provider log. Nothing outside the temporary directory and the run directory was changed.
failure.next: Give failure-handoff.md, run.log and the provider logs to a coding agent to diagnose the first failing criterion. A refusal names its precondition: sign in (codex login or opencode auth login), put the binary on PATH, or note that Decision 0082's window closed. Rerun with --keep from a terminal to inspect the fixture.
